question: What is suzetrigine (Journavx), approved by the FDA in 2025, and why was it notable?
text:
**Suzetrigine (Journavx)** is a prescription, non-opioid pain pill that the FDA approved on **January 30, 2025**, for **moderate to severe acute (short-term) pain in adults**, including pain after surgery. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-novel-non-opioid-treatment-moderate-severe-acute-pain?utm_source=openai))

It was notable because it was **the first FDA-approved painkiller to selectively block NaV1.8**, a sodium channel that helps peripheral sensory nerves transmit pain signals. Unlike opioids, it doesn’t act on opioid receptors. That gave clinicians a new way to treat acute pain without exposing patients to the risks of taking an opioid, such as addiction and overdose. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-novel-non-opioid-treatment-moderate-severe-acute-pain?utm_source=openai))

In two post-surgery trials, suzetrigine relieved pain better than placebo, but it was **not shown to outperform hydrocodone plus acetaminophen**. Its approval was for acute pain, not chronic pain. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-trials-snapshots/drug-trials-snapshots-journavx?utm_source=openai))
